To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methamphetamine is detectable in fingernail specimens collected from amphetamine users.

the concentrations of amphetamines detected in nail clippins are lower than that found in the first 1,5 cm sections of the hair collected from the same subject, and the concentration of the drug in the nails decreases in a manner similar to the drug concentration in the hair.
1) methamphetamine is detectable in fingernails for a period of at least 12 weeks, and 2) the concentrations of methamphetamine in fingernails and hair are comparable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
establishing the feasibility and utility of using fingernail clippers to obtain specimens for the analysis of amphetamine use in the general population.
the development of an analytical procedure to quantitatively analyze nail clippings for the presence of amphetamines.

the development of a method to determine methamphetamine and amphetamines concentrations in fingernail samples and to determine their usefulness for the detection of drug abuse and for the estimation of drug use patterns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results obtained in this study demonstrate that nail clippings can be used to detect methamphetamine and amphetamines, and that these data are reflective of recent use.
the analysis of fingernail clipping and hair sections is a valid and useful method for the determination of methamphetamine use.
methamphetamine and amphetamines can be detected in fingernail samples and hair samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nail analysis is an important tool in the detection of drug abuse.

the nail clippin analysis is useful in providing a qualitative indication of amphetamine/methamphetamine use and the extent of use, but the hair section analysis is a more reliable method of providing quantitative data for the determination of drug use patterns.
nail clippings may be useful for the retrospective detection of methamphetamine and/or amphetamine use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concentrations of methamphetamine/amphetamine in nail clipping samples are comparable to those in hair samples.
fingernail clippers can be used as an adjunct to the analysis of hair specimens for the detection of amphetamine/methamphetamine use.
the concentrations of methamphetamine in the nail samples are generally lower than those in the hair samples, but the concentration ratios are similar.
